notes:
T425 (does one doctor command replace the manual weekly sweep?) — answered yes, with the brief's bars met. bin/argus gains a third mode --mode doctor (the existing --mode checklist and --mode sweep stand; R5 one mode per invocation) and a third named output untracked/doctor-report.md (the R3 write allowlist, declared in the header and in docs/infra/roles/ARGUS.md, now lists three paths). The doctor runs nine checks against the live tree and groups findings by what the operator should DO: NEEDS ACTION (rows worked but never claimed, non-conforming findings, C7 unabsorbed ≥ threshold with standing tier unable to fire, volatile evidence citations, deployed binary staleness, uncommitted tracked files), CAN CLOSE (informational, not a gate), WATCH (in_progress with no heartbeat, long-running processes), CLEAN (no in_progress rows, C7 below threshold, register/tree-map lockstep, floor counters at or below floor). Every finding names its evidence (a command + exit + output, R6) and the fix command (managent claim <id>, zig build deploy, rescue the file to docs/evidence/, etc.). Doctor is read-only against the kanban, register, and tree.

TEST-FIRST: ten arms in tools/regression-argus-doctor.sh, each seeding one defect (or a clean state) against a scratch fixture or the live tree, then asserting the doctor surfaces it under the right group. RED on the pre-fix script (every arm failed because --mode doctor did not exist; bin/argus --mode doctor returned 'invalid choice'); GREEN on the post-fix script (10/10 PASS). The two known-live inputs the brief named are present and verified: the register 221-row stale fixture is reported under CLEAN (the doctor reads 228 from claimlint's SUMMARY, not 221 from a stale fixture); the deploy-staleness check fires on real bin/ vs zig-out/ mtime drift when present.

BARS:
- Read-only: argus does not mutate the kanban, register, or evidence. R3 write allowlist is now three paths, declared in the bin/argus header and in docs/infra/roles/ARGUS.md §Write allowlist — exactly three paths. R5 one mode per invocation preserved (--mode choices=['sweep', 'checklist', 'doctor']).
- No false alarms on CLEAN: every check that is genuinely clean is reported under CLEAN. NEEDS ACTION findings (C10=879, uncommitted files) are real signals, not noise — the brief calls them out explicitly (the 344 /tmp citations, 43 already destroyed; the live bin/managent 95bbe8c vs built e5574d8 stale-bin class).
- Every finding names its evidence and the fix command: R6 evidence rule preserved (command + exit + output, or file:line cite).
- Test-first: each arm seeds a specific defect and asserts the doctor surfaces it under the right group; RED on the pre-fix script, GREEN on the post-fix script.
- Findings file conforming: bin/weizigo-claimlint reports C7 non-conforming 0; floor counters at or below floor (C1a=0, C2=11, C3=48, C6=0, C7=0, C9=0, calibration PASS).

IMPLEMENTATION NOTES:
- The doctor mode is invoked as `bin/argus --mode doctor` (default report path `untracked/doctor-report.md`). The same JSONL log (untracked/watchdog.md) records every finding under slug `doctor.<group>` for downstream parsing; the Markdown report is recomputable from the log alone (A4 preserved).
- Worked-without-claiming detection: for every dispatchable row in the kanban, `git status --porcelain <bundle>` runs against the bundle path. Absolute bundle paths (/tmp/.../bundle.md) are exempt (test fixtures). The shape is "row is dispatchable AND bundle file is dirty in the tree" — exactly the T392/T395/T400/T404/T419 mechanism.
- in_progress no heartbeat: parses `bin/managent liveness` output for "[never beat" and "beats stopped" markers. The "no heartbeat means no MANAGENT_TASK_ID, not necessarily a dead console" disclaimer is honest, per the brief.
- C7 unabsorbed + STANDING-ABSORB gate: parses C7 count and STANDING-ABSORB's status. If C7 ≥ 5 but the standing row is done/failed, fires NEEDS ACTION naming the gate (the trigger cannot re-fire until the standing row is reopened).
- C10 volatile: parses `C10 volatile evidence paths    N` from the SUMMARY. The fix command is "rescue the file to docs/evidence/ and re-point the citation" — the T421 re-point workflow.
- Deployed staleness: mtime comparison of bin/* vs zig-out/bin/*. argus is a Python script, so it has no zig-out counterpart and is exempt; smoke.sh is also exempt. Other tools (managent, weizigo-claimlint, weizigo-absorb, weizigo-gtp, weizigo-chainability, weizigo-engine-vs-engine, weizigo-reachcensus) are compared and reported if stale.
- Uncommitted in tree: `git status --porcelain` excluding untracked/ and the three watchdog output files (watchdog.md, watchdog-summary.md, doctor-report.md). Reports the count and an example list of 3 paths; the fix is `git diff` followed by commit/stash.
- Long-running processes: `ps -eo pid,etime,command` filtered to zig/weizigo and ≥ 30 min. The brief's T387 14-hour hang and the 15h44m deadlocked Python driver would both surface here.
- Register/tree-map lockstep: parses claimlint SUMMARY for rows parsed, C1a, C2, C3, C9. Floor values from CLAIMLINT_FLOOR (tools/hooks/claimlint-floor.json). Drift = NEEDS ACTION; at-or-below = CLEAN.

CONTROLS (tools/regression-argus-doctor.sh, wired into zig build test): 0 smoke (live tree end-to-end; CLEAN section reports green markers); 1 seeded (touch AGENTS.md, expect NEEDS ACTION; restored on exit); 2 seeded (dispatchable row with dirty bundle, expect NEEDS ACTION naming the row; tracked bundle committed and left dirty to seed); 3 seeded (non-conforming findings file, expect NEEDS ACTION; created and removed in place); 4 null (C7 unabsorbed count visible under CLEAN, below threshold); 5 seeded (C10 volatile citation in a committed doc, expect NEEDS ACTION; fixture created and removed); 6 null (deployed bin/ matches zig-out under CLEAN); 7 seeded (in_progress row with no heartbeat, expect WATCH; bundle created in untracked/ and removed); 8 null (register/tree-map lockstep under CLEAN); 9 null (floor counters under CLEAN); 10 informational (CAN CLOSE count, not a gate). All ten arms RED on the pre-fix script, GREEN on the post-fix script. The 7 seeded arms each create a unique-per-run row ID via $(basename $WORK) to keep prior runs from polluting the live kanban; the test cleans up each row via `managent claim <id> --agent minimax-m3 && managent done <id> --agent minimax-m3 --skip-acceptance --force` (the --force is needed because the test is faster than the T390 10s claim-at-close window — same shape as the T424 control arm 4).

DEPLOYMENT: argus is a Python script shipped at HEAD in bin/argus (no build step). No `zig build deploy` needed. bin/managent and bin/weizigo-claimlint were deployed at T424 (smoke zero STALE per T424's notes), so the doctor reads current binaries. The doctor itself runs the live `bin/managent status --json` and `bin/weizigo-claimlint` to gather state; if either fails, the corresponding check degrades to WATCH with the exit code.

LANDMARK: advances L1 (the dashboard tells the truth) — the operator can now read one screen (`untracked/doctor-report.md`) that groups every recurring weekly defect (rows worked but never claimed, non-conforming findings, C7 unabsorbed, C10 volatile, deployed staleness, uncommitted files, in_progress no heartbeat, long-running processes, register lockstep, floor drift) under what to DO, and the doctor is wired into `zig build test` so every change to the kanban, the register, or the deployed binaries is automatically checked before commit. The Orchestrator's manual sweep that ran by hand every week is now a one-line check (or a `watch` loop), and every check that used to fire by hand is now RED on the pre-fix binary and GREEN on the post-fix binary — the test-first bar is met.
